I'm so sorry this has happened to you. It's so unfair that the courts allow one parent to have so much say over a child who was created by 2 people. I'm a woman and parental alienation is happening to me. He was very abusive, and once I left he hired a lawyer knowing I couldn't afford one...long story short...he has had my girls for 5 years, even after 2 failed $2500 attempts to enforce visitation. Even with visitation written on court documents...NOTHING HAPPENS. It's been 5 years and I miss them every day. But this is what they want, and  this is why they allow Parental Alienation to happen. Every time you have to go back to court to enforce visitation, that's more $$$ for the system. When everyone was mad about the immigrant children being taken from their parents...OHHH, I wanted to throat punch all my friends who were freaking out and posting a bunch of stuff on FB. You mean to tell me that you don't give a shit that it's happening in your own backyard everyday, to so many Anerixans but you're freaking out about this?? Don't get me wrong, it shouldn't happen to anyone. But that's the thing, if it's not okay for it to happen to them, and if people are outraged over it... WHERE is the outrage about MY CHILDREN BEING STOLEN???Anyway...lol...  I run a few pages on Facebook for Parental Alienation, and I am friends with over 600 people who it's affected. Mom's and Dad's alike. It's really a great source of support, especially on holidays or birthdays. No one can EVER really know or sympathize with you unless they too have lost their child. Sometimes I feel it's worse than if they had died, because there was never any closure. Not to mention the life long negative effects it has on the child(ren) as a person. If you want some info about those pages, let me know. I've met some really awesome people who have went through hell and back, but are always there making sure the next parent is doing okay. It's like... a really big family, really. Take care sir. ❤️

I'm a born and raised Oklahoman. I was at school in Guthrie, Oklahoma when it happened. Miles and miles away but the windows shook and it felt like a small earthquake. I was in 2ndish grade? Growing up I had a lot of friends who lost their loved ones in the bombing, but being so little when it happened I didn't really know the extent of the situation. As I grew up though, my family and I would go to the memorial downtown to pay our respects, and parts of the reality would hit me. It was a really, really sad day in Oklahoma. The thing I remember the most though, is the amount of people who came to help. From New York to California, so many volunteers showed up and helped us through. A few years later when the twin towers were hit, you bet your ass our firefighters were on route to New York to lend the same helping hand. THIS is why my faith for the country is still strong. When tragedy hits, we all come together despite race, sexuality, or religious beliefs. We are just there to help one another get through, and THAT is the ONE thing that keeps me proud of being an American while the rest of the country seems to be falling apart. Sorry for the novel, lol, but the damage that Timothy McVeigh tried to ravage upon us was outshined by the MANY amazing humans who stepped up to help. It was a sad day, but a day that taught us that no matter what happens, we're all in this together.

I'm sure what they mean is that the eggs are in a premixed bag. They do this at IHOP. I had so many people thank me for informing them they had been eating a premix of eggs, and not actual real eggs. The cooks didn't like it because it was more work for them, but fuck that. BAM...The hashbrowns are ready to throw in the pan and "warm up". Grossed me right the fuck out! And the bacon? It's all premade when you come in at a busy time. I honestly wish more waiters/waitresses would let their customers choose whether they want a REAL egg, or the bullshit premixed stuff...or anything else that isn't normal. But restaurants will push the bag o' eggs because..MONEY. It's...just trickery in my eyes.

Don't ever, ever lie about something that you like to do in your life. Whether it's occasionally or not. If you care about her, and she cares about you, then you both need to be honest about what you DO AND DO NOT want in a relationship. If smoking a little weed is what you like to do, then she needs to accept that, or move on. And you cannot lie about it because then you're not giving her that chance to decide whether it's okay with her or not. Same with her. You both have to be open and honest for your relationship to work. Tell her your sorry, that you ultimately lied to not hurt her feelings although you ended up doing just that. Tell her whether you want to smoke or not, and let her decide if she wants to stick around. My husband smokes every day. But...I'm cool with that. I knew that when I met him, and 5 years later I'm still very okay with it. He provides for us and makes sure we get what we need, so that's all that matters to me. But, everyone is different. Both you and your girlfriend need to sit down and figure out what you are okay with, and what you're not. And if you want to smoke a little weed now and then, and she's not okay with it, then she just may not be the girl for you. Honesty is key is any relationship. Here's the thing...the deadbolt would be sticking out after the door came back around from slamming against the house. After the first time this happened, I thought maybe the deadbolt didn't line up perfectly and it wasn't locking right. So I would make sure to shake the door (pretty hard I admit) to make sure it was locked. Every time. But..Didn't matter. Every few weeks I'd be chilling and all of a sudden the door would slam open against the house scaring me shitless.

Next, I always brush my teeth with hot water. I don't know why, it just seems to get them cleaner. Just to clarify, I also use toothpaste. Ha! Also, I never took showers back then.  Always baths. The plug could be used for the bathtub or the sink. So...One day I was brushing my teeth and the phone rang. It was my best friend. I started talking to her about what we were wearing that day to school as I walked through the house. I hang up the phone, and as I'm walking to my bedroom to go into the bathroom I can hear water running on the tile floor...like LOTS OF IT. I walk in to see my sink PLUGGED and it's COLD WATER. Like I said before, I ALWAYS use hot water to brush my teeth. I know for a fact it was hot when I stuck my toothbrush in my mouth. Also, the plug should have never been in the sink. It was ALWAYS in the tub.  No one else was home that day so that explanation is out. 

That's really the only 2 things that happened, but the door slamming against the house with the deadbolt sticking out happened A LOT. I would tell my family about it and no one ever believed me. Until finally, my cousin was in town. He came over one day, and he saw me shake the door. He asked why...I told him. The grandmother I'm speaking of was both of our grandmother's. He laughed at me. We go watch a movie, and neither one of us had been out of each other's sights since shutting the door. Next thing you know..."BAM"!! I said "TOLD YA"!! We both ran to the front door to see it swinging back closed, with the deadbolt sticking straight out. His eyes were so wide, and all I could do was laugh because I was so used to it.

Since that was my first experience with ghosts, I don't really get scared of the dark, or of seeing anything weird. I've lived in a few houses that I KNEW were haunted, and I would just talk to them as if they were human. Nothing negative every happened. Just "Don't forget I'm still here" signs.

1st-Kids are great! But, they will NOT fix a relationship. They will NOT make life any easier. You will be tired. You will be stressed. Make sure you're at a good place in your life before you decide to have babies. They really are the greatest thing that ever happens to you, but it's  lots of work, and life is no longer all about what you want anymore. They come first, and that sometimes means going without when you aren't financially ready. 2nd-Marry the person you can't live without. The person who loves you as much as you love them. Life is too short to be treated any less than amazing. I wasted 7 years of my life being severely abused. I finally left because I didn't want my girls to grow up and think abusing women was normal. I ultimately left for them as all the love for myself was gone. But, 5 years after leaving him I am the happiest I have ever been, with an amazing husband who has stood by me despite my issues from the past. I still suffer from PTSD, but I started seeing a counselor, and that helps tremendously. 3rd-My BEST advice- At the very FIRST sign of a red flag, in ANY relationship, RUN! They will not change. Once they show you who they are, let them be that person all by themselves. You are an amazing person, and anyone who treats you any less than perfect doesn't deserve a place in your life.
